title: Evaluating and Explaining a Model
audience: Basic science researchers new to AI
objectives: Locate the point where a model stops generalizing and starts memorizing.
Choose a cross-validation strategy that protects the minority class.
Audit per-stratum performance and recognise when a stratum is too thin to judge.
Explain a model globally with SHAP and one prediction with LIME.
Test a model counterfactually against domain knowledge.

sections.name: Dataset selector
sections.purpose: Choose the cohort all four activities share.
sections.how_to_use: A dataset selector, not a track selector: the real eICU cohort is messier; the synthetic cohort has a known ground truth. One split and one scaler follow from this choice.

sections.name: Activity selector
sections.purpose: Four activities behind one segmented control at the top of the page.
sections.how_to_use: Click a chip to switch activity. The dataset, split, scaler, and the logistic-regression model audited in Activity 3 and explained in Activity 4 are all built once above the selector.

sections.name: Activity 1 - Overfitting and Tuning
sections.purpose: Locate the point where a model stops generalizing.
sections.how_to_use: Set a low k and a high k to compare decision-boundary contours, then raise 'maximum k to test' to plot train vs. test accuracy. The dashed line marks the best test k; the train-test gap at k=1 is reported as a metric.

sections.name: Activity 2 - Validation Strategies
sections.purpose: Choose a folding scheme that earns the number you report.
sections.how_to_use: Set folds and model complexity to see the accuracy distribution across folds, then compare K-Fold against Stratified K-Fold, including their standard deviations. LOO-CV is explained in the caption rather than computed.

sections.name: Activity 3 - Subgroup Fairness
sections.purpose: Split the test set and check whether the model serves every stratum.
sections.how_to_use: Pick a subgroup variable and drag the two-handle slider to set the stratum boundaries. The per-stratum table reports accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Strata with fewer than 5 positive cases are flagged unestimable and excluded from the sensitivity spread.

sections.name: Activity 4 - Explaining Predictions
sections.purpose: Explain the model globally, one record locally, and by counterfactual.
sections.how_to_use: SHAP summary plot (set how many features to display), LIME for a single test record (set its index), and a what-if simulator: move the feature sliders and watch the prediction and probability change.

chatbot_guidance: The basic track opens on the synthetic cohort, where the known ground truth makes overfitting easy to see; the learner can switch to the real eICU cohort, which is messier.
In tab 3, moving the stratum boundaries changes how unfair the model looks. That is the point: strata must be chosen for biological reasons and stated in advance.
A stratum with fewer than five positive cases is flagged unestimable, because a single record swings sensitivity from 0.00 to 1.00.
SHAP explains the model, LIME explains one prediction, and the what-if simulator tests whether either agrees with what the learner already knows.
Every chart on this page has a 'View chart data as text (accessible alternative)' expander beneath it, holding the same numbers as a table.
